problem: People and organizations need one local-first workspace where durable human-and-agent work, adaptive software, shared semantic state, and consequential execution remain governed, reconstructible, and verifiable.
outcome: Woyengi composes software around intent and executes durable human-and-agent work toward verified outcomes while preserving the existing persistent-state foundation.

active_milestone.name: Full-product Wave 2 intelligence and application runtime

definition_of_done: Every ticket passes its automated acceptance checks.
Canonical state can be replayed and reconstructed without relying on disposable indexes.
The modular-monolith API, worker, storage, search, eventing, synchronization, SDK, and inspection surfaces are runnable locally.
Adversarial state benchmarks and production-readiness gates pass.
Human QA is acknowledged for the final release candidate.
architectural_invariants: Canonical history is append-oriented and replayable.
Valid time and transaction time are distinct.
Observations, claims, and projected state are distinct representations.
Conflicts remain inspectable even when a projection selects a value.
Agents propose writes; they do not silently redefine authoritative state.
Domain concepts enter through versioned domain packages, never the platform kernel.
Indexes and projections are rebuildable from canonical records.
Identity, workspace isolation, authority, semantic history, provenance, canonical commit, execution journal, evidence identity, and verification-result semantics are constitutional.
Runtime, semantic, and external effects are distinct and consequential external effects are never replayed merely because a provider returned.
Software definitions, workspace data, credentials, and authority remain separate.
Personal and organization workspaces use the same additive product model.

tickets.title: Bootstrap the executable platform repository
acceptance_criteria: The repository declares Node 24 and pnpm workspace constraints.
The architecture constitution and contributor workflow are present.
A single command discovers and executes TypeScript tests.

tickets.title: Define domain-neutral canonical state records
acceptance_criteria: Observations, claims, evidence, provenance, authority, lifecycle, and bitemporal intervals have explicit types.
The kernel contains no Memory, Software, Regulation, Audience, Hospitality, or Forge domain concepts.
Records use stable opaque identifiers and immutable public shapes.

tickets.title: Append claims to an immutable in-memory ledger
acceptance_criteria: Appending a claim never mutates an earlier record.
The ledger rejects duplicate record identifiers.
The ledger can return the transaction-time history of a subject and predicate.

tickets.title: Project bitemporal state with authority and conflict traces
acceptance_criteria: Queries distinguish what was recorded at a time from what is now known to have been valid at that time.
Verified higher-authority claims outrank confidence alone.
Superseded and retracted claims remain historical but do not govern current state.
Every result exposes candidates, conflicts, and an inspectable selection trace.

tickets.title: Replay canonical records deterministically
acceptance_criteria: Replaying the same ordered records produces byte-equivalent projected state.
Replay can stop at an explicit transaction-time boundary.
Projection indexes can be discarded and rebuilt without information loss.

tickets.title: Add reversible identity merge and split operations
acceptance_criteria: Aliases and external identifiers resolve through provenance-backed operations.
Merge and split history is replayable.
Ambiguous identity matches remain provisional until confirmed.

tickets.title: Define the versioned Domain Package extension contract
acceptance_criteria: A domain package can register predicates, event types, lifecycle rules, reducers, verifiers, permissions, and reconstruction policies.
Package compatibility is checked before activation.
A sample package proves extension without modifying the kernel.

tickets.title: Return a structured reconstructive workspace
acceptance_criteria: A request is compiled into explicit state requirements.
The response separates current state, history, evidence, contradictions, permissions, and provenance.
Every reconstruction includes a deterministic trace.

tickets.title: Add compiler type-check and package boundary gates
acceptance_criteria: A pinned TypeScript compiler checks every package under strict settings.
Build and test commands run from the workspace root.
Package imports remain acyclic and explicit.

tickets.title: Define canonical events, relationships, artifacts, and decisions
acceptance_criteria: Events represent participants and valid temporal boundaries without product-specific types.
Relationships and decisions are immutable bitemporal records.
Artifacts retain exact source and residual-detail locators.

tickets.title: Generalize the canonical ledger across record kinds
acceptance_criteria: One append-only port accepts all canonical record kinds.
Duplicate identifiers are rejected globally.
Queries preserve deterministic transaction ordering and record-kind filters.

tickets.title: Build provenance DAG traversal and invalidation propagation
acceptance_criteria: Derived records expose upstream and downstream dependencies.
Invalidating a source identifies every affected record and projection.
Cycles and references to missing records are rejected.

tickets.title: Build evidence support, contradiction, and verification state
acceptance_criteria: Evidence can support or contradict claims with exact locators.
Verification outcomes retain verifier, method, time, and provenance.
Evidence summaries remain explainable and do not mutate source records.

tickets.title: Build contextual authority evaluation
acceptance_criteria: Authority policies evaluate principal, predicate, purpose, context, and time.
Authority remains independent from confidence and evidence strength.
Every evaluation returns an inspectable rationale.

tickets.title: Build capability-based permission evaluation
acceptance_criteria: Capabilities constrain principal, resources, operations, purpose, sensitivity, conditions, delegation, and time.
Read, reconstruct, propose-write, verify, execute, export, and share are separately authorized.
Default denial and permission-leakage tests pass.

tickets.title: Build the extensible verification engine
acceptance_criteria: Schema, constraint, temporal, authority, consistency, external, human, and domain verifiers share one protocol.
Verification failures are explicit results rather than hidden exceptions.
Verification decisions are appendable canonical records.

tickets.title: Build typed graph registry and federation
acceptance_criteria: Graph definitions declare node/edge types, invariants, temporal behavior, retention, permissions, and verification hooks.
Graph registration is versioned and rejects incompatible definitions.
Materialized graphs rebuild from canonical ledger records.

tickets.title: Build cross-graph binding traversal
acceptance_criteria: Bindings connect records across registered graphs without duplicating objects.
Traversal applies direction, depth, temporal, and permission constraints.
Binding traces explain every traversed path.

tickets.title: Build reusable procedure definitions and guarded execution
acceptance_criteria: Procedures define preconditions, operations, tools, invariants, verification, postconditions, and repair behavior.
Execution checks permissions and verification before state-changing operations.
Successful runs can propose versioned candidate procedures.

tickets.title: Define storage ports and durable local adapters
acceptance_criteria: Ledger, graph, object, search, vector, and cache ports are explicit.
A durable local ledger and object store survive process restart.
Adapters preserve deterministic ordering and atomic append semantics.

tickets.title: Build transactional event bus and subscription delivery
acceptance_criteria: Every committed state change produces a typed platform event.
Subscribers resume from durable cursors without silent loss.
Duplicate delivery is detectable and handlers can be idempotent.

tickets.title: Build the ingestion fabric and connector envelope
acceptance_criteria: Documents, events, API payloads, agent proposals, and human actions enter through one typed envelope.
Ingestion records source identity, content hash, storage policy, and transaction time.
Idempotency prevents duplicate source ingestion.

tickets.title: Orchestrate lexical, vector, graph, temporal, entity, state, procedure, and evidence retrieval
acceptance_criteria: Retrieval providers share a scored candidate protocol without becoming canonical memory.
A planner can activate multiple retrieval modalities and fuse deterministic results.
Every candidate retains modality and provenance.

tickets.title: Build semantic decomposition and entity-resolution proposals
acceptance_criteria: An observation compiles into proposed claims, events, relationships, evidence links, and identity candidates.
Compiler output is provisional and retains exact source spans.
No compiler or model output silently mutates governing state.

tickets.title: Build state-requirement planning
acceptance_criteria: Intent resolution identifies subjects, actions, time, domain, constraints, evidence needs, and unresolved contradictions.
Plans declare required graphs, retrieval modalities, authority, and permission checks.
Planning is deterministic for an equivalent normalized request.

tickets.title: Build guarded agent proposal and action protocol
acceptance_criteria: Agent reads and writes require distinct capabilities.
Agent outputs enter as proposals with validation, authority, lifecycle, and optional human verification.
Executed actions retain request, permission, procedure, result, and provenance.

tickets.title: Publish Domain, Agent, and Connector SDK contracts
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose stable versioned contracts without importing service internals.
Examples compile for a sample domain, guarded agent, and idempotent connector.
Compatibility and deprecation behavior is documented and tested.

tickets.title: Build the Platform HTTP API
acceptance_criteria: INGEST, STATE, RECONSTRUCT, and CONTROL API families are runnable locally.
Requests authenticate a principal and enforce capability checks.
Errors, idempotency, pagination, and trace identifiers use stable envelopes.

tickets.title: Build TypeScript and Python client SDKs
acceptance_criteria: Both SDKs cover ingestion, state, reconstruction, control, and subscriptions.
Generated or shared contract fixtures prevent language drift.
Retries never duplicate idempotent writes.

tickets.title: Build storage policies and local/cloud/hybrid synchronization
acceptance_criteria: Every state object can declare locality, regions, devices, agents, encryption, retention, and expiry.
Synchronization uses object-specific merge policies rather than forcing universal CRDT semantics.
Authoritative conflicts stop for explicit resolution while mergeable content converges.

tickets.title: Propagate deletion and source invalidation through provenance
acceptance_criteria: Deletion or invalidation enumerates dependent observations, claims, projections, reconstructions, and notifications.
Retention policy distinguishes logical invalidation from physical erasure.
Unauthorized deleted content cannot leak through indexes or reconstructions.

tickets.title: Build replay, inspection, migration, and backup CLI
acceptance_criteria: CLI replays a workspace until a transaction-time boundary and exports deterministic state.
Operators can inspect provenance, conflicts, permissions, and reconstruction traces.
Migration, backup, restore, and integrity-check commands round-trip test fixtures.

tickets.title: Build Woyengi Explorer
acceptance_criteria: Explorer inspects entity claims, events, relationships, history, evidence, provenance, authority, lifecycle, conflicts, graph neighborhoods, and reconstructions.
Reconstruction traces expose activated graphs, filtering, selection, and unresolved contradictions.
Responsive and accessibility checks pass.

tickets.title: Build admin console and developer diagnostics
acceptance_criteria: Operators inspect connectors, policies, verifiers, subscriptions, storage health, and failed jobs.
Dangerous operations require explicit confirmation and produce audit records.
Diagnostics reveal no unauthorized sensitive payloads.

tickets.title: Instrument traces, quality metrics, and audit events
acceptance_criteria: Metrics cover entity resolution, temporal state, provenance, authority, supersession, conflicts, reconstruction, freshness, verification, and permission leakage.
Trace and metric records avoid sensitive-content leakage.
Audit events correlate request, principal, decision, state change, and reconstruction.

tickets.title: Build adversarial state and reconstruction benchmarks
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover stale state, wrong identity, wrong authority, contradictions, missing evidence, supersession, future leakage, poisoned memory, unauthorized memory, chronology corruption, and invalidated sources.
Benchmarks report correctness and permission-leakage metrics.
Release gates fail on regressions beyond documented thresholds.

tickets.title: Package modular-monolith services and background worker
acceptance_criteria: Platform API and worker compose ingestion, state, reconstruction, verification, policy, sync, and event modules without network calls between them.
Jobs are idempotent, retryable, and observable.
Service boundaries can be extracted without changing public contracts.

tickets.title: Provide local Docker deployment and operational runbooks
acceptance_criteria: A documented local deployment starts API, worker, durable database, object storage, and search dependencies.
Health, readiness, graceful shutdown, backup, restore, and migration paths are exercised.
Secrets are externalized and no development credentials ship in images.

tickets.title: Complete security hardening and threat-model remediation
acceptance_criteria: Threat model covers identity, ingestion, storage, reconstruction, agents, sync, APIs, and operator surfaces.
Authentication, authorization, input validation, audit, secrets, dependency, and data-leakage checks pass.
All high-severity findings are remediated or explicitly rejected with rationale.

tickets.title: Pass final production readiness and human QA gates
acceptance_criteria: Build, type-check, unit, integration, benchmark, security, backup/restore, and end-to-end checks pass from a clean clone.
Release documentation states supported deployment, limitations, rollback, and incident procedures.
Human QA explicitly acknowledges the release candidate.

tickets.title: Establish full-product constitutional contracts and status matrix
acceptance_criteria: The full brief is mapped to implemented, partial, and missing subsystems without overstating readiness.
ADRs fix plane ownership, workspace boundaries, effect classes, execution traceability, runtime dependencies, and App portability.
Implementation status records evidence, limitations, tests, dependencies, and lane ownership.

tickets.title: Create account, workspace, principal, and membership contracts
acceptance_criteria: One account can own a Personal Workspace and participate in Organization Workspaces through explicit memberships.
Human, Agent, Service, and Automation principals have separate identities and cannot silently inherit another principal's grants.
Workspace and organization identifiers are opaque, validated, and immutable.

tickets.title: Enforce workspace isolation and workspace switching
acceptance_criteria: Every governed operation carries an explicit workspace context and cross-workspace access defaults to denied.
A member can switch between authorized Personal and Organization Workspaces.
Isolation tests prove records and memberships cannot leak across workspaces.

tickets.title: Build durable multiplayer WorkInstance and WorkEpisode semantics
acceptance_criteria: A WorkInstance persists intent, participants, assignments, activities, outcomes, and an ordered activity stream.
Multiple WorkEpisodes can execute against one WorkInstance without losing handoff context.
Humans and separately granted AgentPrincipals can assign, hand off, take over, suspend, and resume work.

tickets.title: Define the governed execution spine and effect reconciliation
acceptance_criteria: ActionIntent, ExecutionManifest, ExecutionJournal, evidence, verification, accepted outcome, and semantic commit share traceable identifiers.
Runtime, semantic, and external effects are structurally distinct.
Tool success cannot become an accepted outcome without observed-effect reconciliation and required verification.

tickets.title: Build the reactive Composition Runtime
acceptance_criteria: Components with missing requirements remain PENDING and activate only after compatible authorized providers appear.
Provider loss suspends dependents and disposes owned runtime-effect leases without stale references.
Provider recovery never automatically replays semantic or external effects.

tickets.title: Compile App intent into a software requirement graph and blueprint
acceptance_criteria: Natural-language operating intent becomes an AppIntent before implementation selection.
Requirements are represented independently from providers in a SoftwareRequirementGraph.
The compiler prefers do-nothing, reuse, configure, compose, adapt, and extend before generation and emits an inspectable AppBlueprint diff.

tickets.title: Install portable ApplicationPackages as workspace-bound instances
acceptance_criteria: A package definition installs into two workspaces without sharing semantic data, credentials, or authority.
ApplicationInstances bind existing workspace objects and preserve package-version and overlay provenance.
Filesystem export/import and compatibility checks are deterministic.

tickets.title: Create provider-neutral compute workload and node contracts
acceptance_criteria: WorkloadSpec and usage receipt contracts do not encode a specific model, container, or cloud provider.
A local execution provider enforces explicit authority, budgets, and idempotency.
Node registration and capability discovery keep execution separate from semantic truth.

tickets.title: Add durable events, presence, and realtime collaboration contracts
acceptance_criteria: Presence is ephemeral while Work and activity streams remain durable.
Two authorized clients can observe one WorkInstance through resumable event cursors.
Optimistic concurrency conflicts are explicit and public surfaces cannot access internal capabilities.

tickets.title: Build the unified Woyengi shell foundation
acceptance_criteria: The default shell exposes Home, Work, Apps, Inbox, Search, and one Ask/Create/Delegate surface.
Personal and Organization Workspace switching is accessible and responsive.
Advanced constitutional records remain behind inspect mode rather than the default navigation.

tickets.title: Prove the first full-product local end-to-end flow
acceptance_criteria: A seeded account creates Personal and Organization Workspaces, installs an App, shares Work with a second human and an AgentPrincipal, and switches workspaces without leakage.
A consequential episode records authority, manifest, observed effect, evidence, verification, accepted outcome, and verified semantic commit under one trace.
Typecheck, unit, contract, isolation, conformance, and fast production gates pass locally.

tickets.title: Build bounded episode capability context and agent knowledge workspaces
acceptance_criteria: An EpisodeCapabilityContext contains only the providers, resources, authority, budgets, and policies applicable to one WorkEpisode.
An AgentKnowledgeWorkspace is reconstructible from governed records and cannot retrieve or write outside the episode's workspace and grant scope.
Context segments retain source, trust class, valid time, transaction time, provenance, and authority-filtering rationale.

tickets.title: Add authority-filtered memory and applicability learning
acceptance_criteria: Memory retrieval distinguishes episodic, semantic, procedural, preference, and failure-condition records and evaluates read authority before ranking.
Successful and failed procedures are learned with explicit applicability conditions rather than global confidence alone.
Revoked, invalidated, cross-workspace, or out-of-time memory cannot enter an episode context.

tickets.title: Implement Harness routing and ApplicabilityEvaluation
acceptance_criteria: Skills, Procedures, models, agents, tools, and providers are candidates until an explicit ApplicabilityEvaluation accepts them for current bindings and context.
Jurisdiction, missing-provider, binding override, known-failure, authority, and budget constraints can reject a relevant candidate.
Harness selection is deterministic for equal inputs and records the chosen candidate, rejected alternatives, budget, and rationale.

tickets.title: Create a scoped provider gateway and first local integrations
acceptance_criteria: Filesystem, Git, generic REST/MCP, and model providers bind behind provider-neutral capability and tool contracts.
Provider credentials remain external to Apps and every operation carries workspace, principal, authority, idempotency, expected effects, and reconciliation metadata.
Provider loss updates Composition Runtime availability without replaying consequential external actions.

tickets.title: Build the shared Surface Runtime and narrow public capabilities
acceptance_criteria: Application surfaces render from shared App and Work state rather than creating a private backend or duplicate semantic identities.
Public and embedded sessions receive narrow expiring capability contexts that cannot expose internal App grants or inspect mode.
Two Apps can render the same semantic object identity with different workspace-authorized views.

tickets.title: Add replay, simulation, cost accounting, and package certification
acceptance_criteria: Episode execution records usage and cost by principal, provider, procedure, workload, App, and trace.
Replay and counterfactual simulation compare strategies without reissuing semantic or external effects.
Failure injection and conformance results produce inspectable package certification metadata.

tickets.title: Deliver offline personal start and self-hosted multiplayer serve modes
acceptance_criteria: A seeded Personal Workspace starts locally without Woyengi-operated services and installs a package from the filesystem.
Team server mode persists state in Postgres-compatible storage and supports two humans plus one AgentPrincipal over a durable realtime transport.
A compute node can run separately from the state server while authority, usage, and effect reconciliation stay traceable.

tickets.title: Prove the coding-first engineering reference vertical
acceptance_criteria: A GitHub issue becomes shared Work, is delegated to a separately granted coding agent, and executes in a governed sandbox.
Code, tests, evidence, independent verification, review, and pull-request publication remain under one trace and accepted-outcome boundary.
Provider failure, human takeover, and resumed agent work preserve durable context without duplicating external effects.

tickets.title: Compose reusable business App collections
acceptance_criteria: Customers, Finance, People, Operations, and Compliance collections reuse shared semantic identities, Work primitives, authority, and surfaces.
Installing multiple collections does not create duplicate Customer, Person, Project, Document, or Money identities.
Each collection ships portable packages, seeded examples, verification contracts, and conformance tests.

tickets.title: Build hospitality, construction, and manufacturing reference solutions
acceptance_criteria: Each industry solution is composed from the constitutional substrate and reusable business packages rather than new platform semantics.
Industry Work, evidence, approvals, external effects, and verification remain inspectable under shared contracts.
Reference packages install, export, update, fork, and certify without crossing workspace boundaries.

tickets.title: Add enterprise identity, policy, residency, and deployment controls
acceptance_criteria: SSO, SCIM, groups, advanced ABAC, approval chains, audit export, retention, residency, BYOC, and air-gap profiles extend existing constitutional semantics.
Enterprise policies narrow authority and deployment placement without redefining Account, Workspace, Work, App, or Semantic Commit.
Dedicated, BYOC, hybrid, split-control, and air-gapped profiles have tested backup, restore, upgrade, and incident procedures.

tickets.title: Implement optional Woyengi Cloud managed operations
acceptance_criteria: Cloud manages environments, releases, channels, fleets, desired/reported state, deployment plans, health, backups, upgrades, rollback, metering, billing, and domains/TLS.
Cloud consumes Platform and Compute contracts and never becomes required for local/self-host core operation or defines semantic truth.
Managed public surfaces and package distribution preserve the same App, Work, authority, and verification model as local deployments.
